questions.answer: I appreciate it, though from a distance. I enjoy visiting exhibitions and admiring how much emotion an artist can [[convey]] in a single piece, even if I can't create anything like it myself.

questions.q: What kind of art do you like?
questions.answer: I'm most drawn to traditional Bangladeshi art, particularly the colourful rickshaw paintings you see everywhere here. They're bold, cheerful and full of detail, and I love that such [[intricate]] work decorates something so ordinary.

questions.q: Are you good at drawing or painting?
questions.answer: Not really, I'll admit. I enjoy looking at art far more than creating it. My drawing skills are fairly [[rudimentary]], so I happily leave that to more talented people.

questions.q: Did you do art at school when you were a child?
questions.answer: We had art classes in primary school, and I remember enjoying them even though my pictures were fairly clumsy. It was a nice break from memorising facts, and it let us be a bit more [[imaginative]] than usual.

questions.q: Do you think art is important in education?
questions.answer: Absolutely. Art encourages children to think creatively and express feelings they might not have words for yet. Sadly, it's often [[sidelined]] here in favour of subjects seen as more practical, which I think is a real missed opportunity.
